observations: Photo 0: a square aluminium worm gear speed reducer with a finned grey housing, sitting on cardboard.
Photo 0: a round silver motor input flange with bolt holes and a keyed hollow input bore facing the camera; a hollow output bore on the side of the housing.
Photo 0: an oil plug on top of the housing; cover bolts look uniform and unmarked.
Photo 0: no nameplate, brand, frame size or ratio is readable; the nameplate side is not shown.
Photo 0: clean, no visible cracks, rust or oil leaks; no motor attached; nothing shows it turning.
Photo 0: watermark 'Posted on Jiji STEVE INDUSTRIAL', a dealer photo.

identity.kind: worm gear speed reducer (motor gearbox), small aluminium housing
read_from: photo 0 finned square housing with motor input flange and hollow output bore; no nameplate readable

claims.claim: This is a motor speed reducer
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a worm gear reducer housing with a motor input flange.
Origin cannot be shown by a photo.
No clip of the reducer turning under a motor or by hand.
No clip with sound of it running.
A reducer carries no hour or distance counter; the phrase fits a car part, not this item.
Cover bolts look clean in photo 0, but that does not prove the housing was never opened.

risks.risk: Frame size and gear ratio are unknown and set much of the value.
risks.proof: Sharp photo of the nameplate showing frame size and ratio, plus a photo beside a tape measure.
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest common frame size

risks.risk: Worn worm gear, play in the output, noisy bearings or no oil inside.
risks.proof: Clip of the input shaft turned by a motor or by hand with the output turning smoothly, with sound, and the output rocked to show backlash, with the seller's handwritten note in shot.
Close-up of both shaft seals and the underside after a run.

proof_requests: Sharp photo of the nameplate with frame size and ratio.
Clip of the reducer turning under a motor or by hand, with sound and an output backlash check, with a handwritten note showing today's date.
Photo beside a tape measure for size.
Close-up of the shaft seals and underside.
response.reason: Photo 0 plainly shows a worm gear speed reducer, identified by type, so it can be priced at its worst case as the smallest common size and not working; the nameplate and a running clip would raise it.
